title: akitaonrails/ai-memory
claim: ai-memory — long-term memory for coding agents that survives vendor switches: quit Claude Code mid-task, open Codex in the same directory, and the architecture, failed approaches and open questions carry over. Rust, MIT.
why_good: Everyone builds memory inside one agent; this makes memory a neutral layer between vendors — exactly what devs juggling Claude Code + Codex need. And it's real engineering, not a prompt pack: 40 contributors, 374 commits/30d, packaged for Linux/macOS/WSL2, from a well-known developer educator (Fabio Akita).
value: 商业价值: the vendor-neutral memory store is a natural per-seat team product — shared project memory, sync, retention policy — sold from the same budget as the agent seats it protects.
risk: Anthropic and OpenAI are shipping first-party memory; a cross-vendor layer only matters while multi-agent workflows stay the norm. If one agent wins, its native memory absorbs this.

zh.claim: akitaonrails/ai-memory —— 给编码 agent CLI 的长期记忆,并支持在不同 agent 厂商间交接。
zh.why_good: 给编码 agent CLI 的长期记忆 + 跨厂商交接(1275★、40 贡献者)——让你在 Claude Code/Codex 间切换而不丢上下文,真实的摩擦。
zh.value: 给用多个 agent、想要可携带上下文的团队卖托管记忆服务 + 团队同步。
zh.risk: 记忆正被 agent 原生吸收,而交接只在多 agent 并存时才有意义。
